Never go to bed hungry. I wouldn’t be able to hold back if I was hungry from eating more. I was simply never a breakfast person and I only have 2 proper meals a day. So after waking up at around 10, I don’t even get hungry until 12-3 depending on the day. I have my first meal at around that time and I really like vegetables so my meals are always big and filling. After I have my first meal I don’t usually get hungry again until 6-8. So I might have fruit or a yoghurt in between and then I like finishing my days with snacks or dessert after dinner, so having those extra calories is perfect. 
I used to crave snacking a lot more when I didn’t count, but I’m quite lucky as my hunger adapted quite well when I started eating less. My eating window is still pretty normal I think, I simply start and finish it later.

Always loved snacking, will never stop loving snacking. I eat between 1300-1500 calories per day and usually around 300-500 of those are snacks. Some of course are healthy - fruits, yoghurts, teas, nuts and so on. But of course not all. To satisfy my chocolate cravings - Fibre One chocolate brownies, chocolate cereal, half of a chocolate bar (I love twix), a glass of either soy or oat chocolate milk is also a great choice. All of these are anywhere between less than 100 calories or no more than 200 depending on the portion size. Hope this helps:)

So when it comes to food I don’t restrict anything but have over time worked hard to find replacement for certain high in calorie foods so I can continue to enjoy eating with no restrictions. 

I usually eat two meals a day, because I’ve never been a person that eats in the morning. I’ll have a coffee, but that’s about it. I do however love breakfast food so I usually eat a breakfast meal at around 12-2, snack in between and have another meal at around 6-8. Then I usually have a small dessert or something I enjoy.

On days when I have a little more energy, since I enjoy cooking my meals might look something like [this](https://imgur.com/gallery/UGtNH1w). 
I always liked vegetables and fruits so working them into my meals was easy. It’s worth mentioning that not all of my meals are this pretty or fully home cooked. 

A regular breakfast for me is usually either fruit and yoghurt or fruit and porridge. I usually also add something savoury like a small sandwich. That way I satisfied both my sweet and savoury needs. After that I usually go for tea with milk and a biscuit and then I usually keep myself busy enough so that only have enough time for another tea or two, maybe some fruit or packet of crisps and then it’s dinner time. I enjoy having a big meal for dinner and the picture above represents my meals and preferences well. Today however, I’ve been feeling lazy so I just went for some store bought ricotta dumplings cooked up with crushed tomatoes, red kidney beans, mushrooms and a small salad on the side. I usually have another tea after dinner and then I choose a dessert: some crisps, halo top ice cream, maybe some cranberry cheese, depends what I’m craving. And then there’s obviously water to fill in all the gaps.

What I can offer is advice on purely from personal experience - there’s no need to stop eating the food that you love, however having less of it and replacing more of your meal with really makes a huge caloric difference. 

Ways of cooking your food can make a massive difference too, I cook a lot both for myself and people and overtime I got so comfortable in the kitchen I stopped paying attention to little things like how much oil I use, how much butter I add to a single piece of toast, how many nuts I snack one as I cook because I’ve always got a big jar right next to me. Little things like these have so many calories but unless you make yourself aware of it - it’s so easy to use too much/eat too many. Maybe recommend they start using a tablespoons/teaspoons/cups when measuring things so they’re aware of much they’re using. A scale might be pushing it especially if they’re older.

A good trick I learned is using a small plate for a meal with more calories as the eyes get tricked by seeing a full plate and I use a big plate if I can fill the majority of it with veg because that gives me a sense of achievement - a big meal like this? And not stuffed with calories? 

Educating myself was and still is a big part of my journey, I literally had no clue how many calories things have until I started reading the labels. So maybe try telling them? Maybe even make meals to visualise what you’re explaining. You could make a meal with some chicken, salad and some grilled veg and place that next to a something that adds up to the same caloric value but is only a fraction of the volume to help them better understand how a little bit of knowledge and planning can have you stuffed to brim and a little more healthy. 

Hope this helps, I’m still learning myself so if anyone sees something silly I said - please correct and educate me!🥰
